fatal_flaws: It replaces Picta's colours instead of mixing them in, which overrides the user's binding pick ('tones get MIXED INTO Picta's sky and light'; 'Picta's look stays'). From 06:30 to 20:00 every sky, fog, cloud and ambient hue becomes Astralite's as authored. Picta's blue IMGS frame tint is set to grey. Rain, fog and snow weathers drop to Astralite's neutral grey (sat 0.00). In daylight Picta survives only as cloud shapes, brightness and night, so the user would likely read it as 'Astralite with Picta's clouds', not as a baby of both.

Two brightness levers that the Darkened fix restored are reversed by default. fVolumetricLightingIntensity goes from 0.0 to 1.0 in a copied plugin ini; the 10-12 sweep listed this value as one of about 15 brightness sources. Fog far distances are densified by default (FOG_DENSITY 0.5: B03/C03 go from 150k to 44k, plus E05/E06), which partly undoes the Darkened revert of the misty-weather distances. Direct-light luma is also off by up to 14.4% (C04), and by up to 8% in clear weathers.

The 'summer work stays' pick is broken. The summer files get the same grey filters and the same Astralite clear records, and DirectLightingDesaturationDay goes from 0.6 to 0.0. The warm-summer versus other-seasons distinction from the 10-16 tune is erased.

Night was not offered, yet Night record bytes are rescaled (x m, 0.49-1.0) with filters divided by m. E11 output is identical, but any raw-record consumer (water reflection, LOD; still an open question) sees darker night bytes. Interior-period filters divided by m are applied to the new Astralite day records, so interior output is not truly identical either, though it is mostly inert.

The master STRENGTH dial is a hue lerp, not an amplitude: A01 dawn goes 251 -> 278 -> 330 deg across 0.3/0.6/0.9. Yet the design offers it as the knob for 'too strong'. That breaks the HARD RULE color-strength-not-tone: lowering it on a 'too pink' complaint would rotate the hue back to blue, which is exactly the 08-20 mistake.

Half of pick 2 is missing by default. Astralite's volumetric fog (VOLI) is deferred to an opt-in 'Stage 3' that is OFF and limited to 4 fog weathers. The user explicitly picked 'volumetric fog added to Picta's weathers'.

At the 0.6 default, the Astralite dawn/day/dusk signature is weak. The lerp in normalised RGB chroma passes through the desaturated midpoint (horizon sat 0.57 -> 0.39 lavender-violet, never coral). Dawn/Dusk sunlight, the sun disc and the sunward glow are all left Picta. The user could easily read it as 'Picta with purple dawns plus a few mist rings'.

This is conditional, not fatal as specified. Delivery of the volumetric fog rests entirely on an engine inference: that VL is alive under fVolumetricLightingIntensity=0.0 because bVolumetricLightingUpdateWeather=1 and E11/SkySync/VL multiply renderData in place each tick. That inference is plausible from Effects11.cpp 729-735 and VolumetricLighting.cpp 314-331, but it is unproven, and there is no fallback branch. If the probe shows VL is dead, half of pick 2 silently disappears.

fatal_flaws: It replaces Picta's daytime hue outright instead of mixing it. KAPPA only pulls Astralite chroma toward grey and never back toward Picta's blue, so a true Picta/Astralite mix does not exist. At KAPPA 0 the baby is grey, not Picta. Rain and fog weathers lose Picta's mood by design: D02 dawn light goes from 13 deg/1.00 to 226 deg/0.22. That conflicts with the binding picks 'Picta stays the base' and 'tones mixed into Picta's sky and light'.

By default it moves brightness levers the user fought for. It ships a baby plugin ini with fVolumetricLightingIntensity=1.0, which the 10-12 Darkened sweep had restored to 0.0. It cuts B03/C03 far fog from 150000 to 44232, which partly undoes the Darkened de-mist. It sets the IMGS tint to grey on 30 copies, a change to Picta's own grade. Direct-light luma drifts up to 14.4% (C04).

It adds weather-transition cross-terms that Picta does not have. Records and filters now both vary per weather, and Night records are scaled by a different m per weather (A01 sky top 0.624). The product lerp(R)*lerp(F) therefore no longer matches, and 'night identical' only holds when no weather transition is running: at mid-transition a clear-to-rain change at night comes out about 5% brighter. Interior identity is also not shown for daytime, when the interior reads the Astralite-hued Day record through a Picta/m filter.

VOLI amplitude ignores GAMEVOLUMETRICRAYS RangeFactor. Effects11.cpp 734 multiplies rangeFactor; Picta A01 Day is 0.1 against Soul 1.0, so the transplanted daytime air has a 10x shorter range than in the Astralite lane.

Its only strength dial, STRENGTH, is a tone mix that moves hue: the A01 dawn horizon goes 251 / 278 / 330 deg at 0.3 / 0.6 / 0.9. The design still offers it as the knob for 'too strong'. That breaks the binding rule 'too strong is fixed by amplitude only, never tone'.

As specified it under-delivers pick (2). Astralite's coloured volumetric fog (VOLI air) is off by default as Stage 3, and even when on it covers only 4 fog weathers. On the colour side, a linear chroma lerp of family-averaged donors gives desaturated lavender-violet at the default 0.6 (horizon 278 deg/0.39, fog 298 deg/0.34), not Astralite's coral.

Two double-tint paths remain. WEATHER901 is not retargeted, so the 4 vanilla tundra IDs (NAT coloured records) get the re-hued B01 filters. In Stage 3, GVR ColorFilter stays tied to Picta's DLF (blue 0 at dawn) on top of coloured Astralite VOLI.
